<reason>B more convincingly distinguished useful conservation incentives from a reliable shortage-management backbone. It acknowledged both price responsiveness and enforcement uncertainty, while exposing A’s unsupported comparison between reliably effective tariffs and inevitably fading bans. B also defeated A’s fairness example: universal pool-and-lawn bans spare the careful apartment. A conceded that point but continued recycling the original framing, and its answer to continued excessive withdrawals remained another price increase rather than protection during the adjustment period.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s observation that tariffs can miss the water target even with perfect compliance—because paying is compliance—directly undermined A’s “budget with a dial.” This sharpened the unresolved supply-risk question without pretending restrictions enforce themselves.</best_rebuttal>
